title: Self-Practice Checkpoint — Duality & Principle Deflections (Page 111)
topicTitle: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle and concept of probability
notes: **Q1. Distinguish between an orbit and an orbital.** An orbit is a definite circular path of the electron (Bohr model), planar and described by one quantum number n. An orbital is a three-dimensional region of high probability of finding the electron (quantum mechanics), described by three quantum numbers (n, l, m) and obeying the uncertainty principle.

**Q2. What is the physical significance of the wave function ψ and of ψ²?** ψ itself has no direct physical meaning; ψ² gives the probability density of finding the electron in a small volume around a point, which is used to map the electron cloud.

**Q3. Why did the wave-mechanical model replace Bohr's definite orbits?** Because the uncertainty principle forbids knowing position and momentum simultaneously, a definite orbit is impossible; the electron must instead be described by a probability distribution (orbital).
